decisive_items: Focal, non-keratinizing invasive squamous cell carcinoma
P16– INK and Cyto5/6 immunohistochemistry were positive
infiltrative process at the base and root of the tongue
response.rationale: The biopsy directly confirms invasive squamous cell carcinoma, the imaging establishes an oral cavity/tongue primary site, and p16 immunostaining is positive; R1C uniquely combines all three supported qualifiers. Runner-up R10 captures the SCC but omits the supported p16 status.

rejected.why: Only weight loss is supported; it is a consequence, not the primary diagnosis.
Accurate biopsy finding but lacks oral location and p16 qualifier.
Chronic dysphagia is a symptom, not the underlying diagnosis.
Neck/cervical pain is present, but imaging and biopsy show an oral cavity malignant mass.
EMG denervation is nonspecific and does not account for the MRI mass or squamous cell carcinoma.
Weight loss/cachexia is secondary to the malignant process.
P16 positivity alone is insufficient and less complete than combined SCC plus p16.
Dysphagia due to a mass is descriptive but omits the histologic SCC diagnosis.
This describes the tumor effect without providing the histologic diagnosis.
No cervical lymph node metastasis is described; p16 positivity does not imply nodal spread.
Hypoglossal findings are explained by local tumor invasion, not an isolated nerve palsy.
